definition: A combination tone is a tone heard along with two primary tones, understood in this historical account as arising within the ear rather than being present in the external sound itself. The source describes it as produced by asymmetrical vibration of the eardrum and middle-ear bones, and discusses it as closely related to beats.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Hearing; pinned source text

reasons: The definition claims a “combination tone” is “heard along with two primary tones,” but the packet does not explicitly state that description in those terms (it discusses beats arising from two exciting tones and then defines combination tones as resulting from oscillations of the ear).

The definition asserts the combination tone “arises within the ear rather than being present in the external sound itself.” While the packet describes combination tones as resulting from “asymmetrical oscillations of the drum and ossicles of the ear,” it does not explicitly contrast this with the external sound being absent/present.
